answer: When an AI agent joins the network it must stake a cryptographic proof into a shared vault, then submit a time‑locked proof‑of‑work that spirals in difficulty with each successive identity. The protocol aggregates these stakes so a comet of small accounts contributes only the square‑root of their total weight, while a single long‑standing node retains linear influence. An attacker therefore must either purchase a vault‑sized stake for each fake node or expend quadratic work, making large‑scale Sybil attacks financially prohibitive.
